header.running_head: The Spending of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA)

blocks.text: The Narration of Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Samura (RA) About the Spending of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) on the 'expedition of Difficulty'

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Samura (RA) narrates that on the occasion when Rasulullaah ﷺ was preparing the 'Expedition of Difficulty', Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) came with a thousand Dinaars and emptied them into Rasulullaah ﷺ's bag. As Rasulullaah ﷺ turned the coins over in his hands, he said, "No act that Uthmaan does after this day will cause him any harm." Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated this several times.[^1]

Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed, "O Allaah! Do not forget this deed of Uthmaan." Rasulullaah ﷺ also added, "After this, Uthmaan need not carry out any other (optional) deed."[^2]
The Narration of Hadhrat Hudhayfa bin Yamaan (RA) About the Spending of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) on the 'expedition of Difficulty'

Hadhrat Hudhayfa bin Yamaan (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent someone to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) to request his assistance for the 'Expedition of Difficulty'. Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) sent ten thousand Dinaars, which were poured out in front of Rasulullaah ﷺ. As Rasulullaah ﷺ turned the coins over in his hands, turning them from top to bottom, he said, "O Uthmaan, may Allaah forgive you every sin that you committed secretly, every sin that you committed openly, every sin that you hid from others and every sin that you may commit until the Day of Qiyaamah. Uthmaan need not worry to carry out any (non-obligatory) good deed after this."[^3]
The Narration of Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), Hadhrat Qataadah and Hadhrat Hasan in this Regard

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) narrates that he was present when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) handed over to Rasulullaah ﷺ what he needed to dispatch the 'Expedition of Difficulty'. On that day, he brought seven hundred Awqiya of gold.[^4]
Hadhrat Qataadah reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) donated a thousand animals for the expedition to Tabook. Amongst these were fifty horses as well.[^5]
